...added to raw wool and applied. Olympias of Thebes added hyssop and nitre. Drinking the ash of a deer's horn is also beneficial for a laboring womb. An application of bull bile with two <term>obols</term> <gloss>small weights or coins</gloss> of opium is also helpful. It is useful to fumigate the womb with deer hair. They report that female deer, when they sense they are pregnant, swallow a small stone; this stone, found in their excrement or in the womb (for it is found there too), keeps the fetus safe when tied on as an amulet. Small bones are also found in the heart and womb which are very useful for pregnant women and those in labor. Regarding the pumice-like stone found in the wombs of cows in a similar way, we have spoken of it in the nature of cattle.

Wolf fat applied softens the womb. It is also effective against pains in those parts. It is beneficial if someone who has eaten it is near a woman beginning labor. Indeed, its mere arrival can be harmful <note>implying it might induce labor too quickly</note>. The use of the hare is also of great benefit to women. A dried lung, taken in drink, aids the womb. Its liver taken in water with <term>Samian earth</term> <gloss>a medicinal clay from Samos</gloss> stops discharges. Its rennet helps with the afterbirth, though they avoid bathing the day before. Applied with saffron and leek juice on a fleece, it expels a dead fetus. If the wombs of hares are taken in food, it is believed they conceive males; this is also achieved with their testicles and rennet. 

A fetus taken from a hare's womb is said to bring restored fertility to those who have ceased to bear children. Furthermore, a healthy hare is good for conception, and they give it to the man to drink more often. Also, nine grains of its dung given to a virgin keep the breasts firm forever. The same is done with its rennet. For this reason, it is smeared with honey on the skin where they do not want plucked hairs to grow back. 

For inflation of the womb, it is beneficial to apply the dung of a wild boar or a sow with oil. More effectively, the flour of dried dung can be sprinkled in a drink to stop torments in pregnant or post-partum women. Sow's milk drunk with <term>mulsum</term> <gloss>honeyed wine</gloss> aids women's labor. Drunk by itself, it refills the failing breasts of nursing mothers. If smeared with the blood of a female pig, the breasts grow less. If they are painful, they are soothed by drinking donkey's milk, which, taken with added honey, also aids their purgations. The aged fat of the same animal heals ulcerations of the womb, and when applied on a fleece, it softens hardness of the womb. Used by itself, fresh or aged and applied with water, it has the power of a <term>psilothrum</term> <gloss>a hair-removing paste</gloss>. The aged spleen of the same animal applied with water causes an abundance in the breasts. 

It beautifies the face. A fumigation with a donkey's hoof matures the fetus so as to even call forth an abortion; it should not be used otherwise, for it kills a living fetus. If the fresh dung of the same animal is applied, it is said to wonderfully settle discharges of blood. Likewise, the ash of the same dung applied is beneficial to the womb. 

Horse foam applied for forty days before they are born suppresses the first hairs. Likewise, deer horn does this. It is better if the horns are fresh. The womb is aided by being washed with mare's milk. If a dead fetus is felt, the spleen drunk in sweet water ejects it. Likewise, a fumigation of the hoof or dried dung. Butter infused stops a prolapsed womb. Bull bile mixed with oil of roses opens a hardened womb when applied externally on a fleece with turpentine resin. They also say that a fumigation of dung from a male ox represses a prolapsed womb and aids the fetus. 

Conception is aided by drinking cow's milk. It is certain that sterility can be caused by the trauma of childbirth. Olympias of Thebes affirms this is corrected by bull bile and snake fat with verdigris and added honey, applied to the medicinal areas before intercourse. Calf bile, if used during purgations and sprinkled on the womb during intercourse, softens hardness of the belly, reduces discharge if the navel is pricked, and is generally beneficial to the womb. They set the measure of bile at one <term>denarius</term> weight mixed with a third part of smallage and as much almond oil as seems sufficient; this they apply on a fleece. 

The bile of a male calf ground with half as much honey is kept for the womb. If they eat roasted calf meat with <term>aristolochia</term> <gloss>birthwort</gloss> around the time of conception, it is promised they will bear males. Calf marrow boiled in wine and water with tallow is beneficial for ulcerations of the womb. Likewise, fox fat and cat excrement applied with resin and rose oil. 

They think it most useful to fumigate the womb with goat horn. The blood of wild goats with "sea palm" <note>likely a type of seaweed or coral</note> removes hair. The bile of other goats, when sprinkled, softens callosity of the womb and causes conception after purgation. Thus, the power of a <term>psilothrum</term> is also achieved if applied for three days after the hairs are plucked. Midwives promise that a discharge, however immense, is stopped by drinking goat urine, or if dung is applied. The membrane of goats, aged after the birth is produced and taken in wine, expels the afterbirth. 

They think it useful to fumigate the womb with the hair of kids. In a discharge of blood, the rennet is drunk or applied with henbane seed. Aeschines says that if a woman's loins are pricked with the blood of a black wild ox, she will develop a loathing for sexual intercourse. Similarly, he says goat urine drunk with nard causes love. 

Nothing is more useful for infants than butter, by itself or with honey; specifically for teething, the gums, and mouth ulcers. A wolf's tooth tied on prevents the fears of infants and diseases of teething. A wolf skin provides the same. Indeed, their largest teeth tied to horses are said to provide an untiring course. An infant's bowels are settled by hare's rennet applied to the breast. Donkey liver with a little <term>panace</term> <gloss>all-heal herb</gloss> dripped into the mouth protects infants from the falling sickness <note>epilepsy</note> and other ills. They prescribe this for forty days. A donkey skin thrown over them makes infants fearless. The teeth that horses lose first, when tied on, provide easy teething for infants, more effectively if they have not touched the ground. 

Calf spleen is eaten in honey or applied for pain of the spleen. For running ulcers, it is used with honey. Calf spleen boiled in wine, ground, and applied, heals sores of the mouth. A goat's brain passed through a gold ring and dripped into the mouths of infants before they taste milk protects against the falling sickness and other infant diseases. Goat dung tied in a cloth restrains restless infants, especially girls. Gums smeared with goat milk or hare brain make teething easy. 

Cato thinks that sleep is induced by taking hare in food. The common people also believe it brings grace to the body for nine days—a trivial saying, yet there must be some reason beneath such widespread persuasion. The Magi say that the bile of a sacrificed goat, if smeared on the eyes or placed under the pillow, induces sleep. The ash of a goat horn with myrtle oil inhibits sweats when smeared on. Sexual intercourse is stimulated by applying boar bile. Likewise, swallowing pig marrow. Donkey fat mixed with the fat of a male goose, or even the [semen] from a horse's mating, as Virgil...

<summary>This page details ancient remedies for women's health, pregnancy, and infant care using various animal products, including deer, hares, cows, and goats. It covers treatments for labor, fertility, teething, and common ailments like insomnia and ulcers.</summary>
